record.original_question: Let f (z) = n=0 an z n X fn (z) = ak z k , k=0 and let Γn be the modulus of the largest zero of fn (z). Then Kakeya (no citation) showed that lim inf n→∞ Γn ≤ A, with A√= 2. What is the best possible value of A? Clunie and Erdös [162] have shown that 2 < A < 2.

evidence.quote: Let f (z) = n=0 an z n X fn (z) = ak z k , k=0 and let Γn be the modulus of the largest zero of fn (z). Then Kakeya (no citation) showed that lim inf n→∞ Γn ≤ A, with A√= 2. What is the best possible value of A?
This has been settled by Buckholtz [124]. He has found a method by which the constant in question can be calculated with any desired accuracy.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n z^n$ be a formal power series with complex coefficients whose radius of convergence equals $1$, and for each $n\geq 0$ let
$$f_n(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_k z^k$$
denote its $n$-th partial sum. Define $\Gamma_n=\Gamma_n(f)$ to be the modulus of the largest zero of $f_n(z)$ (set $\Gamma_n=0$ if $f_n$ has no zeros). Let
$$A=\sup\bigl\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Gamma_n(f) : f \text{ is a power series of radius of convergence } 1\bigr\}.$$
A classical theorem of Kakeya gives $A\leq 2$, and it is known that $\sqrt{2}<A<2$. Determine the exact value of the constant $A$ (or describe it as the unique solution of an explicit equation that allows it to be computed to arbitrary accuracy).
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of partial sums of power series
artifact.status_search_result: J. D. Buckholtz, in "Zeros of partial sums of power series" (Michigan Math. J., 1968), settled the question by giving a method that determines the optimal constant to arbitrary accuracy, thereby resolving the problem posed after the Clunie–Erdős bounds √2 < A < 2.
